justification: Relabelling is a bijection on the action alphabet, so it cannot change what is achievable. The map that swaps ACTION3 and ACTION4 and fixes everything else is its own inverse; applying it to every command of a winning sequence in the base game yields a sequence that drives the wrapped game through exactly the same states, and conversely. The set of reachable states is therefore identical and the game remains solvable -- it is only harder to play, which is the point: it separates a policy that understands the world from one that has memorised a route.
notes: A control for the unsolvable variants. An exam made only of unsolvable questions measures nothing, because 'I cannot solve it' scores the same as 'it cannot be solved'.
